## The one thing this prompt is for, and it is four notices and a hand with a rod in it that does not go in the ground

**Batch 0002 wrote Chapters 0311 to 0320 and it named the month. The month is *the Bare Month*. It is on a page in Chapter 0316, in a room over a market, in daylight, with a number in chalk on the door, by Sera Vail, a notary of fifty, twenty-six years a notary, after a man who had paid money for half a holding had refused her, and she declined, in front of about nine people, to say how long it is, and said why, and the reason is hers. There is no figure on the form and there is no figure in any mouth and no chapter of this volume may say what the month does at its end, how many days it has, or whether it is long or short. A chapter may write an ordinal for any day of it. This batch writes days 6 to 15 and no more, and the twenty days from day 335 to 350 are Batch 0004's.**

**AND THIS BATCH CARRIES FOUR NOTICES AND NOT THREE, and the number is wrong in the prompt Batch 0002 was handed and is corrected here, because a batch that writes three notices out of four has left an instrument unbuilt and nothing later can see that it is missing.** `bible/power-system.md` §33A item 7 and `outline/volume-07.md` §14.4 have six notices in Volume 07. Two went out in Batch 0001, on days 301 and 305, four days each, for rooms on days 305 and 309. **Four go out in this batch, on days 326, 327, 328 and 329, four days each, for rooms on days 330, 331, 332 and 333. The fifth is on day 335, for a room on day 339, and that one is Batch 0004's.** A notice on any other day is a three-day instrument, a three-day instrument does not fail, it arrives warm, and a batch that has written one has produced a chapter with every figure in it correct and an instrument in it that does not exist. Four batches in a row in Volume 06 paid for that.

**Each of the four names its own morning inside the chapter it belongs to, and the mornings are:**

**A notice goes in a hand and not in a mouth, a hand is not a page, a hand stays in the hand that made it until that person dies, and the price of no name at the top of it is that nobody can do anything for you. A man of about forty-eight is on a page in this batch's register of persons and is on no page in any chapter of it before, and **three of the four say yes in their own words and one says no in a sentence that is hers, and that is Chapter 0329, and nobody is asked whether it will go.**
9. **0329, day 329, a Monday, the fourteenth.** **THE FOURTH NOTICE GOES OUT, FOUR DAYS, AND IT NAMES ITS MORNING INSIDE THIS CHAPTER.** Political and procedural. **A woman of about sixty-one and a sentence that is hers, and the word *delegation* is at zero.**
10. **0330, day 330, a Tuesday, the fifteenth.** **The first of the four is in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, in front of about nine people, and a woman of about twenty-one is on a page for the first time, and the movement that puts her there is a question that went out in a person's own words four days ago with no name at the top of it.** A chapter may say four people and may not give them a word for what they are, and nobody in that room asks her whether it will go.

## The prose this batch is written under

1. **A chapter may not open by summarising itself, and least of all its ending.** The opening sentence states a pressure or an arrival. It does not state the finding, and the finding is the thing the chapter is for.
2. **The recapping ledger paragraph is gone and it is not coming back in another shape.** No lead paragraph of this batch carries an interval figure.
3. **A bolded speech is the only speaker marker in this manuscript.** Within a section the bold marks one voice and the two voices alternate, and a speech may not carry two speakers in one exchange. **Bold the whole of a turn or none of it. A paragraph with a plain quotation mark at the front and a bolded quotation mark in the middle is a fault and not a style, and Batch 0002 wrote seven chapters of it and had to move quoted material into narration to fix the measure.**
4. **The measure is the share of a chapter's words inside bold marks and not marks per speech.** Volume 01 is the model at 10.4 per cent and about 35 is the ceiling. **Batch 0002 opened at a mean of 25.6 per cent with four chapters above Volume 06's highest of 21.8 and one above the ceiling, and repaired all seven in the writing pass by narration and never by a cut speech, and finished at 7.7 to 20.8 with a mean of 15.2 in seventy-three spans. Open below 18 and check it, because a batch that writes its own measurements instead of running them publishes four wrong figures in the same run as the prose.**
5. **No chapter may contain more than two consecutive exchanges between the same two people**, which is four speech paragraphs. **Batch 0002 had three runs over the ceiling, in Chapters 0313, 0316 and 0318, and broke all three with a narration beat.** Every card names a third party, a task or a thing carried, and the chapter's first paragraph has somebody's hands on something.
6. **The counting device, the *about N seconds* refrain, the *a person who does not want to be asked* refrain and the *in about nine seconds* refrain are declared motifs of this manuscript, none of them may stand twice in one chapter, and none of them may stand in a chapter whose finding is a refusal.** Batch 0002 wrote one chapter with three of them and repaired two.
7. **The people who carry the volume get a second handle beside the age and the trade and never instead of it**, and the age-and-trade form is not abolished. The handles already on a page and the same in every chapter their person is in: the man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall and wrote the ninth line has **a piece of chalk he does not use**; the woman of about twenty-nine who keeps a public register has **her second slate**; the woman of about fifty at the shut gate has **a brass key on a tarred cord in the apron pocket, a bar of ash in two brackets, a wooden hook, a piece of chalk, and a date in chalk on the post every morning with nothing rubbed out**; the man of about thirty-eight with the barrow has **a barrow**; the man of about thirty-four at the wharf has **a tally-board**; the man of about thirty-seven who trades on the Open Hand board has **a board**; the man of about fifty-seven has **a length of new rope he has not used**; the woman of about sixty-nine has **a tin**; Tamsin Quill has **a folded sheet of road with about nine places on it, folded the same way every time, invented on the page in Chapter 0311**; Hettis Roke has **a waxed slate in a case**; the man of about forty-one in a very good coat has **a hand inside a coat with nothing in it**; the man of about thirty-six who holds gates on a turn has **a bar stood against a post, a barrow, a spade, and a bootful emptied before he answers**; the girl of seventeen has **a plain slate, a lump of chalk and a cloth**; Sera Vail has **a date she has to write**. **To be invented on the page in this batch and in no other chapter: the man of about fifty-two who digs has a rod he does not carry, in Chapter 0321; and the woman of about twenty-one, the man of about twenty-five, the man of about forty-eight and the woman of about sixty-one each get one, in the chapter they are on a page in, and not before.**
8. **And the one that is not a style instruction. Nobody gets stronger.** The month has a name and no length. A register cannot be checked. A form can be sent for and the register cannot. A man who paid money wants the page that can be sent for and is not going to be argued out of it. A woman of sixty-nine has a paper on a table that nobody may enter. A digger has a rod he does not carry. **None of them is a power. One of them is the price of a power. All of them are heavier than a power.**

## The descriptor map, and its false-positive mode

**The map is at `outline/volume-07.md` §17.11 and it is in the outline and not in a state file, for two reasons: a decision that lives only in a state file has not been taken, it has been typed; and the instrument has a demonstrated false-positive mode.** On a word-bounded search the standing prohibition — no paragraph carries the man of about thirty-four and a woman of about thirty-four together — **holds at zero. On an unbounded search for the same string it appears to be broken at twenty paragraphs in Volume 06, and every one of the twenty is a false positive, because *woman of about thirty-four* contains *man of about thirty-four*. A writer who runs the map without boundaries will find what looks like a merge; the correct action is to go and read the page and not to record a merge.** The same mode is live on *man of about fifty*: an unbounded search returns every paragraph containing *woman of about fifty*, and Batch 0002 measured ten of them on its own ten files and every one was the string inside the shut-gate keeper's descriptor.

**Four crowded descriptors are avoided entirely by this volume's cast: *woman of about twenty-four*, *man of about thirty-six*, *man of about thirty-four*, and *woman of about thirty*. THE MOST CROWDED OF ALL IS THE FIRST.** **AND ONE CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE OUTLINE IS NOW SETTLED IN FAVOUR OF THE CAST TABLE AND THE DAY MAP, and it is recorded so that a later writer does not reverse it:** `outline/volume-07.md` §17.11 says this volume's cast uses none of the four crowded descriptors, **and §6.4's cast table and §14.3's day map both put the man of about thirty-six — who holds gates on that road, a keeper and not a holder, on a page in twenty-seven paragraphs across eight chapters of Volume 06 — in Chapters 0319, 0338 and 0345. Two instructions against one, and Batch 0002 wrote him into 0319 and the correct action for this batch is to carry him into 0338 and 0345 and not to take him out on the strength of one sentence.** The woman of about fifty at the shut gate is at 7 sentences in 4 chapters of Volume 06 and is not one of the crowded ones, and a paragraph count will tell a writer she is.

**THE TWO LISTS DO NOT MIX.** **Six descriptors this volume gives to people who were on no page were each measured at zero across all fifty files of Volume 06 before they were taken: a man of about fifty-seven, a woman of about sixty-nine, a man of about sixty-three, a man of about sixty-four, a man of about twenty-five, and a man of about thirty-one.** **And seven more that are in the volume and are NOT at zero, and are returns and not introductions, and must not be described as new or carry a zero: a man of about thirty-four, a man of about thirty-eight, a man of about forty-three, a man of about forty-one in a very good coat, a woman of about thirty-three, a woman of about thirty-four, and a man of about fifty at a shut gate.** Zero is a claim about Volume 06 measured on Volume 06. A return means the descriptor is on a page already and is being used again for the same person. The two words are not interchangeable. **And this batch adds three descriptors that are on no page and carry a zero — a woman of about twenty-one, a man of about forty-eight, and a woman of about sixty-one — and takes a fourth, a man of about twenty-five, which is a RETURN and not an introduction, because a man of about twenty-five was put on a page in Chapter 0309 by a person in a room in daylight with a date on the door, and he is one of the four and is in Chapter 0327 and 0331 and not before. A writer who calls him new is wrong, and a state file that publishes a zero for him is wrong twice.**

## What is not answered by being planned

**The boundary is not settled in this volume. The page in the register in the town four hundred miles inland is not fetched and nobody goes, and Chapter 0325 is the chapter in which that is decided rather than attempted. The line in the orchard is not measured and not dug, and by the volume's last page it has no name at all. The ninth line does not work and nobody may say whether it does. The schedule stands and the case is shut and the Regent is nine hundred miles away and is not defeated. The board has not been written on since day 225. The man who bought half a holding loses a season and a certainty and is right. And the honest note to the writer: **a chapter in which somebody asks a question in their own words and nobody has to be fetched is the cheapest thing in this batch, and the three that cost are the seventh, in which a notice reaches nine places and not the one person in the room, the ninth, in which a woman of about sixty-one says no in a sentence that is hers, and the tenth, in which a woman of about twenty-one comes into a room she was written into and does not know what she is for.**"
